title: A Atlas for the Bridge
premise: In 1911, in a Baltic port city under shifting imperial rule, apprentice clockmaker Petra Eriksen is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, the civic heartbeat that governs ships, trains, and telegrams. While dismantling its escapement he finds a sealed letter hidden in the case, naming his late father among conspirators who once used the clock to time a smuggling run that ended in a drowned crew. As authorities close in and the workshop faces seizure, Petra must choose between destroying the evidence that would save the shop and preserving the truth of who his father was. He finishes the repair, delivers the letter to the last surviving widow of the drowned crew, and lets the workshop burn — carrying away only his father's smallest tool, finally belonging to no one but himself.
about_author: Orsen Winterbourne is the pen name of a former marine instrument restorer who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse clocks along the northern coast before turning to fiction. He writes about people who measure their lives in small, precise movements against large, indifferent machinery.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Petra Eriksen climbs to the observatory to repair the master clock that regulates the entire port, working alone through the night while the city sleeps below. In the weight case he discovers a sealed letter bearing his father's handwriting, dated the week before the ferry disaster twelve years ago. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: quiet pride curdling into dread as precision work becomes an excavation of the past.

chapters.title: What the Clock Kept
chapters.summary: Petra secretly reads fragments of the letter at night: his father timed a smuggling run by the master clock, and the schedule was sold to customs men who sank the boat instead. The magistrate's clerk begins asking questions about the workshop's ledgers. His mother burns papers she won't explain. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: the sickening realization that inheritance can be a debt, and every tick of the repaired clock is testimony.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Ordered to certify the clock for the naval review, Petra finds the mechanism sabotaged — someone wants the port's timing thrown into chaos during the inspection, framing the Eriksen name for treason. He must rebuild the escapement from memory while soldiers wait downstairs and the clerk offers him freedom in exchange for denouncing his dead father publicly. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: climax — craftsmanship as moral act, hands shaking over the one choice that cannot be undone.

chapters.title: A Atlas for the Bridge
chapters.summary: Petra certifies the clock, then walks the letter to old Marta Voss, widow of the drowned captain, who tells him his father died trying to confess. The order to seize the workshop arrives at dawn; Petra takes only his father's smallest file and watches the fire take the rest. On the bridge at dusk, the harbor bells ring true on the hour. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into release — survival stripped to what can be carried, and carried honestly.
